seo.title: H&M: AI digital twins of models - first campaign live (2025)
seo.meta_description: H&M digitized around thirty real models into AI twins (Uncut studio) to produce ads, social, and e-commerce visuals without reshoots. Campaign live July 2025.
seo.resume_citable: In 2025, H&M created with the Swedish studio Uncut AI digital twins of around thirty real models, who keep ownership and a revenue share, to produce ad, social, and e-commerce visuals without reshoots; first campaign live on July 2, 2025.

faq.q: How many models did H&M digitize?
faq.a: Around thirty real models, turned into AI digital twins with the Swedish studio Uncut. Each model keeps ownership of their twin and can rent it to other brands.

faq.q: Are the models paid and the content labeled?
faq.a: Yes. H&M says the models keep ownership of their twin and a revenue share, with pay aligned to the standard use of their image, and that the AI-generated content is clearly labeled.

pattern: AI digital twins of models for creative production
objectif_business: Produce fashion visuals (ads, social, e-commerce) without multiplying physical shoots, while keeping real models, their rights, and their pay.
description: H&M digitized around thirty real models to turn them into AI-generated digital twins, with the Swedish tech studio Uncut. Each model is photographed from several angles and lighting setups to capture their features and movements, then Uncut produces a usable replica. The twin is then used to compose product visuals and campaign images without organizing a new physical shoot: if a model is already working elsewhere, her twin can wear another collection the same day. The framework is designed to defuse the rights issue: the model keeps ownership of their twin, can rent it to other brands, including competitors, and is paid on a basis aligned to the standard use of their image. AI-produced content is labeled on social media. The first public campaign went live on July 2, 2025 around denim, with twins staged against the backdrop of fashion capitals, co-created with a dedicated team (photographer Johnny Kangasniemi, model Vanessa Moody) and accompanied by a making-of film. H&M announced further AI drops for fall 2025.

resultats.metrique: First public campaign online, denim collection

niveau_preuve.justification: Official H&M Group press release (primary source) confirming the launch, corroborated by several established news outlets naming the brand and the partner Uncut. No financial results isolating the impact of the setup, so no level A; no quantified platform case study, so no level B.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Per campaign and per drop: once the twins are created, visuals are produced on demand without a new physical shoot.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: H&M creative direction and content teams, with the AI partner Uncut for building the twins.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The fidelity of each model's initial scan (angles, lighting, features, movements) and the validity of the rights framework. If the scan is poor, the twin is not usable; if the rights are not framed, the visual is not publishable.

etapes.detail: Photograph each model from several angles and lighting setups to capture their features and movements.
etapes.acteur: H&M creative team and AI partner

etapes.detail: Uncut generates the usable AI replica from the captured data.
Contract the model's ownership of the twin and pay aligned to the standard use of their image.
Compose product and campaign images by dressing the twin, without a physical reshoot.
Publish on social and e-commerce, clearly marking the content as AI-generated.

prerequis_data: Agreement of real models and digitization data (multi-angle scans, lighting, movements)
Asset library to store and version the twins
Product catalog and style reference set to dress on the twins
prerequis_orga: Legal framework for image-rights transfer and model pay
AI Act compliance: systematic labeling of AI-generated content
Alignment between creative direction, legal, and the production studio

playbook.action: Select a small group of volunteer models and frame their rights and pay
Digitize the models from several angles and lighting setups
Produce the digital twins with an AI partner
Generate a first test campaign on one product category
playbook.livrable: Campaign visuals produced without a reshoot

playbook.action: Label and publish on social and e-commerce, then measure perception
playbook.livrable: Compliant published content and audience feedback

replication.equipe: A creative direction, a photo production studio, an AI digital-twin partner, and an intellectual property / image-rights lawyer.
replication.premiere_etape: Select a few volunteer models and write the rights and pay framework before any digitization: this is what makes the setup publishable and defensible.

statut_vivant.note: The setup is real: first campaign live in July 2025 and further drops announced for fall 2025. As of the verification date, no public confirmation of continued active use in 2026 was found, and the initiative remains surrounded by industry debate over jobs in creative fields. To revisit.

transposable_ue.note: H&M is an EU brand (Sweden) and the setup was born in the EU. Key constraints: AI Act (obligation to be transparent about and label AI-generated content), image rights and rights transfer for the models, GDPR for digitizing the person (features, movements). H&M labels AI content and has the models sign ownership of their twin.
